skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render MP4 videos from React and Remotion TSX components through the inference.sh belt CLI. Configure duration, resolution, frame rate, props, composition, and codec.
skill.summary: Turn Remotion component code into configurable MP4 renders through the belt CLI.
skill.author: skills-shell

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown backticks and code fences, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. The meaningful risks are remote submission of TSX and props to inference.sh, inline shell quoting when building belt commands, and one remote Markdown image. No evidence found for prompt injection text or hidden malicious instructions.

remediation.issue: Remote render service receives user code and props.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning that TSX, props, asset URLs, and render settings are sent to inference.sh before rendering.

remediation.issue: Inline shell examples embed large JSON and TSX inside single quotes.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a JSON input file, here document, or structured argument support. Do not interpolate untrusted code into shell commands.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on an external CLI and related install commands.
remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted source, version expectations, and verification steps for belt and related skill installs.

remediation.issue: The documentation embeds a remote image.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local marketplace asset or proxy the image to avoid automatic third-party requests from documentation viewers.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from React Code
content.value_statement: Teams often need repeatable video renders without opening a video editor. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to render Remotion components as MP4 files through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Runs the infsh/remotion-render app through the belt CLI.
Accepts React and Remotion TSX code that exports a default component.
Configures width, height, fps, duration, codec, composition ID, and props.
Uses Remotion APIs such as useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, interpolate, and Sequence.
Returns an MP4 render result and can show streaming progress through the SDK workflow.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Sends component code, props, and asset references to an external service.
Does not provide a local Remotion render pipeline or sandbox.
The TSX must compile and export a valid default Remotion component.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Create short animated text, counters, and transitions from Remotion component ideas.

use_cases.title: Automate Product Videos
use_cases.description: Render release clips or feature explainers from reusable React components and props.

use_cases.title: Generate Data Updates
use_cases.description: Produce recurring chart videos or status visuals from data-driven component inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Basic Intro
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Remotion intro video with centered title text. Render it at 1080p, 30 fps, and three seconds long.

prompt_templates.title: Add Motion Timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Remotion animation with fade-in text, a spring scale effect, and a clean background. Keep the render under five seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Use Props and Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a product update video that accepts title, subtitle, and color props. Use square output, 60 fps, and a concise visual style.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Sequenced Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-scene Remotion composition with timed sections, animated counters, and a final callout. Explain any external assets before rendering.

output_examples.input: Render a three-second welcome animation from a Remotion component.
output_examples.output: The result is an MP4 render link with a short note about resolution, duration, and frame rate.

output_examples.input: Create a square animated counter for a launch post.
output_examples.output: The output includes a rendered square video and a progress update while the render runs.

output_examples.input: Render a prop-driven product title card.
output_examples.output: The result is a downloadable MP4 that reflects the provided title, subtitle, color, and duration settings.

best_practices: Confirm that component code and props are safe to send to inference.sh before rendering.
Start with short, low-resolution renders before producing final high-resolution output.
Keep Remotion components small, deterministic, and explicit about imported assets.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, credentials, or private customer data in code or props.
Do not assume the render is local or offline; the workflow uses an external service.
Do not paste unreviewed TSX into shell commands without checking quoting and escaping.

faq.question: Does this render locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses the inference.sh belt CLI and a remote render app.

faq.question: What input does it need?
faq.answer: It needs TSX code that exports a default Remotion component. Optional props and render settings can customize output.

faq.question: Can I choose video dimensions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents width, height, fps, duration, codec, composition ID, and props.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is sensitive code safe to use?
faq.answer: Treat sensitive code as private data. Review it before sending it to an external render service.

faq.question: What happens if my TSX does not compile?
faq.answer: The render can fail. Test a small component first and fix Remotion or React errors before a final render.
